questions.question: Many products classified as poison are also:
questions.explanation: Many poison products are also flammable. Take proper safety steps if your cargo may be flammable.

questions.question: The correct way to check tire pressure is to:

options.text: Push on the tires to feel the pressure.

questions.explanation: You must check each tire at the start of each trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only way to accurately check tire pressure.

questions.question: Class 7 hazardous materials are:
questions.explanation: Radioactive materials are Class 7 hazardous materials.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials:

options.text: Keep all other vehicles away from the station.

questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials. Someone must stay at the nozzle and watch the fuel flow at all times.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials is to:
questions.explanation: The manual provides the information needed to pass the test. For deeper learning, read and understand federal and state rules about transporting hazardous materials, and take hazardous materials training courses.

questions.question: The correct way to check tire pressure is:

options.text: By pushing on the tires to feel the pressure.

questions.explanation: You must check each tire at the start of each trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only way to accurately check tire pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a shipping paper?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all shipping papers.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, you must park at least ____ away from any building.
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, building, gathering place, or open fire.

questions.question: Hazardous materials may be transported by:

options.text: Any driver, as long as the hazardous materials weigh under 50 pounds.
Any driver in a rural area.
A driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: If a package says "Inhalation Hazard," what placard must be used?
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a package or shipping paper, display a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, you should know that:

options.text: Radiation passes through to other packages.
The package should be placed in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.
The package should be made of wood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation passes through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads around each package and passes through nearby packages. Rules control how many packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: Shipping papers must include:
questions.explanation: Shippers of hazardous materials must include an emergency response telephone number on shipping papers.

questions.question: If you are transporting Class 3 flammable liquids and need to move cargo to another tank, you should:

options.text: Transfer it on the roadway as long as no one is nearby.
Not transfer it on a public road, unless there is an emergency.
Keep it secret when moving it to another tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not transfer it on a public road, unless there is an emergency.
questions.explanation: Do not transfer flammable liquids from one vehicle to another on a public road, unless it is an emergency. Always warn others about the hazards of the materials.

questions.question: On a shipping paper with both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous materials may be identified by being:
questions.explanation: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous items must be clearly marked. They can be listed first, highlighted in color, or marked with an "X" before the description.

questions.question: If you discover your cargo is leaking, you should:

options.text: Touch the leaking material to identify the cargo.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
Assume all the cargo is leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
questions.explanation: If cargo is leaking, identify the materials using shipping papers, labels, or package location. Do not touch the leaking material.

questions.question: Hazardous materials shipping papers may not be kept:

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's door.
In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
Within reach of the driver while wearing a seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be quickly accessible in an emergency. While driving, keep papers in a pouch on the driver's door or where you can reach them quickly while wearing your seat belt. You can place papers on the driver's seat when you are out of the vehicle.

questions.question: The only correct way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tire with your hand.

questions.explanation: Check your tires at the start of every trip and after each stop. Always use a tire pressure gauge to check if tires are properly inflated.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained and tested?
questions.explanation: All drivers must receive training on hazardous materials transportation risks and how to respond to security threats. Training and testing are required at least once every three years.

questions.question: If the third column of the Hazardous Materials Table shows "Forbidden," what should you do?

options.text: Transport the substance only at night.
Transport the substance with a security guard.

questions.explanation: The third column of the Hazardous Materials Table shows hazard classes. Never transport any material marked "Forbidden."

questions.question: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be:

options.text: Inside a gas station looking out a window.
In the vehicle, awake or asleep.

questions.explanation: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be awake in the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. They must know the hazards, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the vehicle if needed.

questions.question: Shippers must label hazardous materials. What should you do if an item is too small for its label?

options.text: You can bundle the item with other hazardous materials and attach a paper label to the outside of the bundle.
You can attach the label to a tag and securely attach the tag to the package.
You can mark the item with a large orange dot.
You can place the item in a box that displays a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can attach the label to a tag and securely attach the tag to the package.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped hazard labels must go on hazardous materials packages. If the label does not fit on the package, you can attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
In the Periodic Table of Elements.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
questions.explanation: The Emergency Response Guide (ERG) from the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) contains information about hazardous chemicals. The guide is organized by shipping names and identification numbers.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The manual has what you need to pass the hazmat endorsement test. However, it does not cover everything needed to do the job safely. Hazardous materials training courses provide additional important information.

questions.question: Who controls hazardous materials laws?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are risky. The federal, state, and local governments all create regulations for transporting these materials.

questions.question: Where should you place a placard?

options.text: At least three inches away from any other markings.
Under a ladder if space is limited.
On a background that is the same color as the placard.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least three inches away from any other markings.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed at least three inches away from other markings. Keep placards clear of doors, ladders, and other attachments. Always place placards against a background with a different color.

questions.question: When can you move a vehicle with improper placards?

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.
If the vehicle will travel less than 10 miles.

questions.explanation: A vehicle must have correct placards before driving. An improperly placarded vehicle can only be moved if it is necessary to protect people or property in an emergency.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: Which agency helps coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards?

options.text: The United Center for Chemical Assistance

questions.explanation: The National Response Center helps police and firefighters coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards.

questions.question: Which agency conducts a background check when you apply for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: When you apply for a new or renewed HazMat endorsement, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts a federal security threat assessment.

questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers be kept when the driver is not in the vehicle?

options.text: In the driver's pocket or bag.

questions.explanation: Shipping papers for hazardous materials must be easy to reach. When the driver is away from the vehicle, leave the shipping papers on the driver's seat.
